name: Popular democracy
summary: Popular democracy holds that political decisions should be made as directly as possible by the people, through referendums and other tools for expressing the popular will, rather than by parliaments or officials. It grew out of populism and links popular sovereignty with civil rights, free debate and, in its left-wing strand, economic democracy and participatory institutions such as participatory budgeting. Its answers on most non-democratic questions are therefore thin and split.
scope: The referendum-based and participatory strand described in Wikipedia's Popular democracy article: Leveller popular sovereignty (An Agreement of the People, 1647-49), Rousseau's sovereignty of the people, and contemporary participatory writers such as Hilary Wainwright and Harry Boyte, with Havel's civil-society model. It excludes the label's use by regimes such as Gaddafi's Libya or Assad's Syria, and it does not cover people's-democracy doctrines of Marxist-Leninist states. Many answers outside democratic procedure are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Hilary Wainwright

keyFigures.name: Thomas Paine
keyFigures.role: Named among the early thinkers in the popular-democracy tradition.

sources.author: Wikipedia

sources.title: Democracy
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Direct democracy, majority rule, Rousseau's general will, sortition and tensions with minority rights.

sources.title: An Agreement of the People (1647 and later versions)
sources.author: Levellers and New Model Army Agitators; as summarised by the Civil War Petitions project (bcw-project.org.uk)
sources.usedFor: A summary of the Agreement's clauses: sovereignty in the people, reserved rights, religious freedom, no conscription, equality before the law.

sources.title: The Social Contract and Discourses (G.D.H. Cole translation, with introduction)
sources.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
sources.usedFor: Popular sovereignty and the general will; only Cole's introduction and chapter list were read, not Book III.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The sources give no health programme; economic-democracy and anti-neoliberal strands imply support for public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the economic-democracy value and the critique of big business in the left-wing strand.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Wainwright strand criticizes neoliberalism and big business; the core idea is silent on markets, so this is inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Left strands favour economic democracy while the Leveller root opposed common ownership, so adherents split on state ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the economic-democracy and anti-big-business strand; no tax programme is stated.

unions-good.rationale: Wainwright's work on a new trade unionism points favourable, though the article notes limits of popular democracy for unionism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Levellers defended property while modern participatory strands favour economic democracy, so the movement is split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Hostility to big business in the contemporary strand implies tighter control, but no regulatory programme is documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the left-leaning participatory strand is critical of neoliberal austerity, so inferred disagreement.

worker-ownership.rationale: Economic democracy is listed among the values; collective worker ownership is one form but is not specified.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Listed civil rights (free speech, inquiry, debate) point against broad surveillance; the topic itself is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on drug policy and adherents hold both views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Free speech is a listed value but equality before the law is too; the sources do not resolve the tension.

strong-leader.rationale: Popular sovereignty in Rousseau's sense rests on the people's own will, not a leader who bypasses it; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Wainwright's aim is to reclaim and democratize the state, not abolish it, and popular sovereignty presupposes a state.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed anywhere in the sources; no principled position follows.

empower-police-military.rationale: Civil-rights emphasis and distrust of elites suggest scepticism, but this is inferred rather than stated.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Outside the scope of the sources; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Participatory budgeting and civil-society models place decisions close to citizens, though referendums also operate nationally.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the civil-rights and equality values.

traditional-family.rationale: Christian popular democrats and left participatory democrats sit in the same label and differ on this.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Equality before the law is a listed value, so inferred mild agreement; adherents were not documented on the topic.

abortion-legal.rationale: Christian-democratic and left strands diverge, and many popular democrats would put it to a vote instead.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian democratic parties used the label but the participatory strand is secular; genuinely split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equality and bias-free values suggest support, though the sources do not describe specific remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A cultural-theory question that popular democracy does not address.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Populist-derived strands lean toward this and left participatory strands do not; no stated position.

gradual-change.rationale: Popular democrats seek deep change through direct participation but by peaceful, procedural means, so split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Majoritarian populism and inclusive civil-society strands pull opposite ways; the sources do not say.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Popular sovereignty, taken from Rousseau, locates authority in the people rather than distant bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: The Wainwright strand is anti-neoliberal and anti-big-business, which suggests scepticism; not stated directly.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; the populist root points to yes but the civil-society strand to no.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No foreign-policy content in the sources.

limit-growth.rationale: Degrowth versus growth is not discussed in the sources on popular democracy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the left participatory strand; the sources give no environmental programme.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Outside the ideology's concerns; some would put it to a referendum.

revolution-justified.rationale: Popular democracy is built on referendums and civil society, as in Havel's model, rather than armed overthrow; Nepal's Maoists are an exception.

experts-over-public.rationale: The idea that decisions made by general referendum are fairer than those of officials or parliaments makes this a central rejection.

central-planning.rationale: Participatory, bottom-up decision making conflicts with central planning, though the economy is not discussed in detail.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic democracy as a value with markets not rejected; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: No fiscal doctrine in the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian economic-democracy leanings; not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; adherents could favour or distrust it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; left and populist strands might favour it, but nothing is stated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Participatory budgeting favours citizen allocation but state direction by officials runs against it; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Leveller tradition upheld small property-holders and economic democracy favours dispersed ownership; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a feature of popular democracy, whose economic ideas are reformist; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No stated position on monetary institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages conflict with direct citizen decision making; inferred, not discussed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anti-partisanship and popular sovereignty are listed values; Nepal's Maoists even moved away from vanguard-party reliance.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Levellers placed sovereign power in the people, not the King, and a hereditary head conflicts with that.

democracy-best.rationale: Popular sovereignty is the theme, but the sources show some strands praise participation over bare electoral democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: The article defines popular democracy as direct democracy using referendums and holds that general referendums decide more fairly than parliaments.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils are not discussed in the popular-democracy sources, though participatory decision making in workplaces points to some sympathy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Self-determination by popular decision supports secession by vote; not stated.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement rests on popular will being superior to elite judgment and on equality before the law.

political-violence-never.rationale: The core is peaceful and procedural but revolutionary regimes also used the label, so adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; civil-society and participatory strands are not militarist.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian popular democrats and secular participatory democrats disagree.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law resting on the people's own decisions is the core principle; scripture-based law would override it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Popular sovereignty implies public, accountable institutions; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: No foreign or defence doctrine in the sources.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equality before the law and civil rights point away; the article notes majoritarian misuse in Sri Lanka.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands accept it and Leveller, civil-society strands do not.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Economic democracy is a value but equality of outcomes is not a stated goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; local self-rule suggests mild sympathy but majoritarian strand differs.

colonial-reparations.rationale: No foreign-policy or reparations position in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Supranational religious or civilizational unions are never discussed in the sources, and referendum-based self-rule gives no lead either way.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rousseau's general will asks citizens to look to the common good over private interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Listed civil rights are central values, so duty over rights is unlikely.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not an attitude of reform-minded participatory democracy.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological speed is not a concern of popular democracy, though a public vote on disruptive change is the likely preferred method.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; a likely referendum topic rather than a settled position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Handing decisions to algorithms displaces citizen decision making, the core of the doctrine; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Civil rights of free speech and inquiry suggest agreement, but the topic is not discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology looks to expanded participation, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold an ideological commitment to popular will but not against pragmatic fixes.

direct-action.rationale: Civil-society movements use protest, while referendum advocates stress formal channels, so split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Participatory strands insist that organizing be democratic, but this is inferred, not quoted.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivism has no place in the referendum and civil-society traditions the sources describe.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Utopian abolition of specialization is absent from the sources, which describe reformist participatory institutions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; left strands might accept, Leveller roots would not.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; economy is not detailed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not in the shared core; a Marxist-Leninist strand would agree, others not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Nepalese Maoist version is described as non-elitist with less reliance on vanguard parties, which is inconsistent with this.

collective-farming.rationale: Not a feature of the ideology; inferred from the Leveller and participatory emphasis on local choice.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Theories of imperialism belong to Marxist-Leninist strands only; popular democracy as a whole has no stated view on the causes of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Participatory budgeting assumes public revenue allocated democratically.

harm-principle.rationale: No source ties popular democracy to Mill's harm principle, and majoritarian voting could set limits on liberty beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rousseau grounds legitimacy in the collective body, though civil rights are also listed; split but leaning no.

conscription.rationale: The 1647 Agreement barred pressing men into service, yet republican strands accept citizen obligation; split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement's whole point is that voice through voting outweighs exit; Rousseau treats the right to vote as the citizen's essential part.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers replaces citizenship with consumption, against popular sovereignty; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Economic democracy and participation imply that material means matter to action; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist roots would agree, but not documented in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equality before the law and bias-free values oppose racial hierarchy; the sources do not discuss genetics.

organic-representation.rationale: Direct popular decision making rejects estate-style representation; not explicitly discussed.

total-state.rationale: Civil rights and free debate are listed values, and popular democracy is opposed to a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The sources show no rebirth or decadence narrative; the label is used by too many differing movements to infer one.

territorial-expansion.rationale: No stated expansionism; civil-society strands reject it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Levellers anchored authority in the people's agreement rather than personal oaths to lords.

bound-labor.rationale: Equality of all persons before the law, as in the 1649 Agreement, rules out legally bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The sources on popular democracy take no epistemological stance on knowledge and power.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral epistemology is not part of the doctrine; Rousseau's general will and Christian democrats point opposite ways.

single-common-good.rationale: Rousseau's general will points to one common good, whereas pluralist participatory strands treat interests as competing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is not discussed in the sources on popular democracy, and a popular-sovereignty principle does not settle it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship is outside the sources, and a participatory view would likely leave the matter to the citizens' vote.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed, and no principle of popular sovereignty settles it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy is listed as a value of popular democracy and participatory decisions in workplaces follow.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; left and right strands split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal macroeconomics is absent from the sources, apart from criticism of neoliberalism that does not settle deficit policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; civil rights are central but economic freedom is not stated.

rule-by-example.rationale: The ideology relies on citizens' decisions and law, not rulers' example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Popular sovereignty carried to the level of a nation; stated by Rousseau for a people, though extension to nations is inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign-policy legality is not discussed; popular democracy has no stated stance on UN authority.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Christian democrats and secular strands both used the label.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants is not covered, and strands that are inclusive or majoritarian would answer differently.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not a stated position; inferred from the left strand's critique of neoliberal welfare reform.

class-collaboration.rationale: Christian-democratic strand agrees, left strand disagrees.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Hostile to destroying cultural institutions; popular democrats value inquiry, debate and civil society.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; regimes using the label (Libya) might agree.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organize nationally or internationally is not an issue the sources address.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equality before the law is a listed value, though the article notes tensions with feminism.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is outside the ideology and no source connects it to popular democracy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equality before the law and bias-free media are listed values that exclude racial classification by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands accept it; civil-society strands treat the state as reclaimable, so split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not part of the doctrine; a popular vote could settle it either way.

elite-replacement.rationale: The ideology is anti-elite but this specific conspiracy claim is not part of it.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1647 Agreement called for representatives elected in proportion to constituency population; support for proportionality of parties is inferred.

national-mission.rationale: No mission doctrine in the sources.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminism's relation to popular democracy is noted as limited in the article; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Popular democracy grew from populism, whose core charge is that elites ignore the people; stated as origin, not as a doctrine.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Equal rights before the law and civil rights oppose coercive eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability to the people follows from popular sovereignty, though the sources do not mention transitional justice.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Economic democracy and participatory budgeting need more than minimal government.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equality before the law and bias-free values are listed as core.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of all persons before the law is in the 1649 Agreement, and equality before the law is a listed value.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is a debate within Marxism-Leninism, and the sources on popular democracy do not take part in it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonial history of states is not discussed in the sources, and popular sovereignty alone does not settle it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality before the law implies one civil law for all; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Agreement bars Parliament from interfering in religion; free inquiry is listed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; a likely referendum question rather than a doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strands split between Christian democratic and secular participants.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Nepalese Maoist popular democracy is described as less party-centred; inferred rejection of a strengthened coercive state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1647 Agreement declared sovereign power to reside in the people, and its design was a contract between electors and representatives.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are absent from the sources on popular democracy.

population-transfer.rationale: Equality before the law and civil rights oppose expelling minorities, though the article notes majoritarian misuse against Tamils.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rousseau's general will stresses solidarity; Social Darwinism is absent from the sources.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The SEP notes democracy cannot remove its own procedural rights; popular democrats hold both views.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The SEP links democratic law with freedom as independence; adherents would accept the idea although not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: The Agreement made Parliament supreme under reserved rights, while populists distrust checks on the popular will; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nepal's popular democracy is described as non-elitist with less reliance on vanguard parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Participatory budgeting is said to raise participation of poorer residents, supporting a pro-poor lean.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed, and left and populist strands could differ.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Wainwright's trade-union work and civil-rights values suggest opposition; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The ideology locates problems in institutions and who decides, not demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Equality values oppose this; not directly discussed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is a direct-democratic device known from Athens, but popular democracy centres on referendums and elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Civil rights are listed as core, though regime users of the label did so.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Emergency price-fixing is not covered by the sources, so no position can be reliably inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bias-free mass media and free speech are listed values.

party-commands-army.rationale: Popular sovereignty and anti-partisanship oppose party control of the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not addressed, and inclusion and majoritarian strands would differ.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not documented; inferred from the anti-elite character, as in recallable-delegate traditions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Rousseau's sovereignty cannot be alienated; popular sovereignty implies reluctance to pool power away.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Leveller Agreement made the people's representatives supreme over the executive.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Popular, participatory decision making implies congregational or elected rule; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rests with the people according to Rousseau and the Agreement, not clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist position; the sources on popular democracy do not discuss it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Free speech, debate and inquiry are listed civil rights.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Anti-elite and referendum-based accountability implies concern with entrenchment; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: The Agreement conceived the representative as a contract renewed at each election, and recall extends this accountability.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed in the sources on popular democracy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; extreme measure beyond the ideology's reformist economics.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; Leveller tradition opposed pressed service but valued citizen militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The agrarian-moral theme is not part of the doctrine, though populist roots mention rural radicals like Jackson.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Self-determination by popular vote supports reunification by referendum, though not stated.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist roots support it, but the participatory strand includes educated activists.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not discussed, and popular democracy has no stated theory of civilizations.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; often handled by referendum.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum is not addressed, and Christian democratic and left participatory strands would split on it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Free inquiry is a listed value; the topic is not discussed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, though free-speech values pull one way and majoritarian morality the other.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not discussed in the sources; it could equally be decided by public vote.

minority-language-support.rationale: Equality before the law suggests support; not stated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Agreement protects religious freedom but equal application of law is also core.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Free speech, debate and inquiry are listed civil rights; the Millian framing is not stated.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-neoliberal strand would sympathize; not documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Postcolonial development debates are outside the sources on popular democracy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Agreement of the People was conceived as a written constitution drawn from the people rather than handed down.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not addressed in the sources on popular democracy.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is not discussed in the sources, and it would be a matter for public decision.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Direct election fits the preference for direct citizen decisions over parliament; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Rousseau and referendum logic would subject institutions to popular will; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; a likely referendum topic.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rousseau subordinates property to the general will but Levellers defended it; split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The debate over the Soviet Union's character is internal to Marxism and not addressed in the popular-democracy sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk doctrine is not part of the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Collective defence treaties are not covered, and popular democrats could back them or demand referendums.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation without the people's consent violates popular sovereignty as Rousseau frames it; applied to territory by inference.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; Christian democratic strand disagrees.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Anti-partisanship is a value, but the sources do not discuss heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Popular sovereignty implies that peoples decide their own status; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are not discussed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereign power resides in the people per the Agreement, which excludes any sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Egalitarian economic democracy implies progressive taxes; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The nature-nurture question is outside the doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Agreement reserved rights the representatives could not override, and equality before the law is core.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not covered in the sources on popular democracy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The ideology gives power to the many rather than mixing it with rule by the few.

leader-cult.rationale: The people, not a leader, is the centre of the doctrine, though some regimes claimed the label.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is not covered in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is a Maoist debate, and the popular-democracy sources only mention Nepal's Maoists moving away from vanguard party reliance.

land-redistribution.rationale: Levellers did not seek common property, while left strands might; split.

refugee-return.rationale: Civil rights and equality imply the right; not stated.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism conflicts with the equal-rights base; not discussed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Agreement barred Parliament from interfering with religion and free inquiry is a core value.

women-must-cover.rationale: Civil rights favor personal liberty; not stated.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary unions are not discussed in the sources; euro referendums showed adherents split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not covered in the sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Local self-government in civil society models supports it; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: This is a diaspora strategy question not covered by the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands would accept it, but popular democracy as a whole is silent.

ban-cartels.rationale: Hostility to big business suggests agreement; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Referendum logic favours the popular will but civil rights are core values and the SEP notes the tension; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; feminism's relation to popular democracy is described as limited.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; autarky is unlikely for the participatory strand.

moral-incentives.rationale: Guevarist moral incentives are not part of the sources on popular democracy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The ideology's means are referendums and civil society.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equality of all persons before the law (1649 Agreement) is incompatible with hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History teaching is not discussed, and popular democrats have no stated curriculum view.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by consent of a people is central; rule by tutelage contradicts it.

patriotic-education.rationale: National loyalty teaching is not covered; populist roots and civil-society strands would split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not addressed in the sources, and equality before the law can be read either way.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary-system reform is not discussed in the sources on popular democracy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Debate over capitalist crisis belongs to Marxist theory and is not addressed in the sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed in the sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theory prescriptions are outside the sources on popular democracy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Leninist theory is not part of the sources on popular democracy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equality before the law as a listed value suggests no; the application to private owners is inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Agreement reserved inalienable rights from Parliament, and listed civil rights are values of popular democracy.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial boundary law is not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Leveller constitutionalism had the people choose representatives at frequent elections, not inheritance.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority decision is the working rule of referenda; the SEP notes Locke treats majority rule as natural.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Agreement reserved rights against Parliament as a limit on rulers' power; resistance itself is inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1647 Agreement made Parliament supreme but popular democracy prefers direct popular votes to parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not discussed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The doctrine depends on equal citizens, not elite duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Participation is the core virtue; withdrawing contradicts the doctrine.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School cultural theory is not part of the sources on popular democracy.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not part of the sources on popular democracy.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is not part of the sources on popular democracy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices by birth are not discussed; equality before the law points one way and populism the other.

notes: Statements on economics, culture and foreign policy are mostly inferred from the left participatory strand; the Leveller root defended property, Christian popular democrats and some regimes differ, so those answers are low-confidence or neutral. The third missing statement rests on the article's note on participatory budgeting; citing Porto Alegre details came from the Participatory democracy article, which was opened but not listed as a source. Fetched summaries came from a summarising tool, not raw page text.
